items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: Johnny St. Cyr used to play with him.

ctx.x: Did you ever know two guys, they called themselves Jack and Jill? Uh... Jack Dowden, he played mandolin. And Jules Batiste, he played guitar?

Oh, Jules Batiste. I heard of him, but that's been nice, a good while now. Yeah. Johnny St. Cyr used to play with him. Johnny St. Cyr was, uh... Was a guitar player too. A fine guitar player too. Yeah. Johnny St. Cyr was... Well, he complimented. He played with Brobyshire's band too, used to... He played with all them, uh... all them big high bands.

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1959-08-11
items.q: Johnny St. Cyr, talking about the same thing.

ctx.x: I think Johnny St. Cyr said he used to use ropes.

Yeah, he used to take, uh, he'd break a string, you know, one of his, uh, string. He'd get an old sash cord and put it on there. And they could rouse him, and rouse him up and put it on there and wind up, go on, let's go. And, you don't tell him you ain't tuned, just let him go, but he's a money getter though. Yeah. Yeah, you see, he could take and, uh, see you'd have a bunch of men, and, uh, he was well-liked. And he'd get a, he could rhyme. See, like you named Mr. Russell, somebody, meet him in the back and…
